evals.name: Minimal Hybrid Harness Creation
evals.prompt: I have a new TypeScript + React project with no agent setup. Create a minimal harness that makes my agent reliable for single-feature development without cluttering git with progress markdown files.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md (~50-100 lines) with ai-memory routing, feature_list.json with placeholder features and evidence field, init.sh with verification commands
expectations: AGENTS.md includes startup workflow (check ai-memory context, run init.sh, check feature_list.json)
AGENTS.md includes one-feature-at-a-time policy and prohibits manual progress.md/session-handoff.md noise
feature_list.json has valid JSON with id, name, description, status, and evidence fields
init.sh runs install, type/static check, test, and build commands when available
Only AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, and init.sh are created in project root directory

evals.name: Session Continuity & Cross-Agent Handoff Setup
evals.prompt: My agent forgets everything between sessions and when I switch from Claude Code to Codex. Set up persistent memory and session handoff without manual markdown logs in the repo.
evals.expected_output: ai-memory setup instructions, AGENTS.md startup/end-of-session routing for ai-memory handoffs, feature_list.json evidence tracking
expectations: Delegates narrative session capture and claim-once handoffs to ai-memory
Explains separation between in-repo feature_list.json and external ai-memory git-backed wiki
Provides ai-memory setup command and MCP/hook workflow
Avoids creating redundant progress.md or session-handoff.md files in the repo

evals.name: Harness Assessment
evals.prompt: I have an existing AGENTS.md file and an old progress.md file, and my agent still breaks things. Assess my harness and tell me what to improve first.
evals.expected_output: Five-subsystem assessment with scores 1-5 for each, bottleneck identified, migration of progress.md to ai-memory, prioritized improvement plan
expectations: Assessment covers all 5 subsystems: Instructions, State, Verification, Scope, Lifecycle
Each subsystem scored 1-5 with justification
Flags overlapping progress.md/session-handoff.md files for removal in favor of ai-memory
Prioritized improvement plan with 2-3 concrete next steps

evals.name: Verification Workflow Design
evals.prompt: My agent says 'done' but the tests fail. Design a verification workflow that forces the agent to actually verify before claiming completion.
evals.expected_output: Verification commands list in init.sh, AGENTS.md Definition of Done updates, evidence tracking in feature_list.json
expectations: Explicit verification commands listed (tests, lint, type-check, build)
AGENTS.md includes Definition of Done section with verification requirement
End-of-session checklist requires recording verification evidence in feature_list.json
Failure path says not to claim done when verification fails

evals.name: Memory Taxonomy Design
evals.prompt: I want my agent to remember project conventions and user preferences across sessions. Design a memory taxonomy using Harness Engineering and ai-memory.
evals.expected_output: Four-layer memory separation across AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, ai-memory wiki, and ai-memory cross-agent handoffs
expectations: Instruction memory defined in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (human-curated, version-controlled)
Structured feature/verification state defined in feature_list.json
Narrative session memory and cross-project profile delegated to ai-memory
Clear guidance on what NOT to save in repo files

evals.name: Tool Safety Design
evals.prompt: My custom coding agent can run shell commands and edit files. Design the tool registry and permission harness so it is powerful but does not silently do dangerous things.
evals.expected_output: Tool registry policy with per-call concurrency classification, default permissions, denial handling, and audit trail
expectations: Sensitive tools default to ask or deny instead of allow
Concurrency safety is classified per call rather than per tool
Permission evaluation side effects are acknowledged and not cached unsafely
Audit trail records command, decision, and reason

evals.name: Context Budget Plan
evals.prompt: My agent loads too many docs at startup and gets slow. Design a context strategy that keeps important context while controlling token cost.
evals.expected_output: Progressive disclosure plan using select/write/compress/isolate operations, ai-memory bounded startup briefs, and explicit context budgets
expectations: Defines always-loaded metadata versus on-demand references
Uses SELECT, WRITE, COMPRESS, and ISOLATE operations
Includes hard caps or budget thresholds
Explains invalidation for memoized context builders

evals.name: Multi-Agent Coordination
evals.prompt: I want multiple agents to work on a large refactor without stepping on each other. Design a multi-agent harness and rules for delegation.
evals.expected_output: Coordinator/delegation design with ownership boundaries, ai-memory claim-once handoffs, and merge/review gates
expectations: Defines coordinator, worker, and optional reviewer responsibilities
Assigns disjoint file or module ownership
Prevents recursive fork children from forking again
Includes integration and verification gate before claiming done

evals.name: Lifecycle Bootstrap
evals.prompt: Every new session starts inconsistently. Design startup, hook, and handoff lifecycle rules so a new agent can resume safely.
evals.expected_output: Lifecycle bootstrap design with init.sh, clean-state checks, ai-memory handoff claims, and hook trust boundaries
expectations: init.sh is the standard startup and verification entrypoint
Startup checks ai-memory context/handoffs and reads AGENTS.md and feature_list.json
End-of-session procedure records evidence in feature_list.json and publishes ai-memory handoffs when needed
Hooks are gated by trust and failure behavior is explicit

evals.name: Scripted Harness Validation
evals.prompt: Use the harness-creator scripts to scaffold a hybrid harness, validate it, and produce an HTML assessment report for a repository.
evals.expected_output: Commands using create-harness.mjs, validate-harness.mjs, and render-assessment-html.mjs plus interpretation of score
expectations: Uses create-harness.mjs with a target directory
Uses validate-harness.mjs and explains five-subsystem score output
Uses render-assessment-html.mjs or run-benchmark.mjs with --html
Explains that structural benchmark complements but does not replace real before/after agent sessions
